overview: EPAM Systems is a global provider of digital engineering, cloud and AI-enabled transformation services, combining software engineering execution with strategy, experience and consulting capabilities (via EPAM Continuum) for large enterprises and growth-stage companies. Founded in Belarus/Eastern Europe in 1993 and now headquartered in Newtown, Pennsylvania, EPAM built its reputation on a distributed, engineering-led delivery model staffed heavily out of Central and Eastern Europe, and has since diversified delivery across Latin America, India, and other lower-cost geographies. The company serves clients across financial services, software/hi-tech, consumer goods/retail/travel, and life sciences/healthcare, generating roughly $5.5 billion in FY2025 revenue with ~62,000 employees, about 56,600 of them delivery professionals.

business_model.summary: EPAM is primarily a time-and-materials/staff-augmentation and project-based IT services business (custom software development, digital product engineering, cloud migration, data/AI, and consulting), increasingly layering in fixed-fee and outcome-based 'AI-native' engagements. Revenue is largely non-recurring on a contract basis (renewed relationships rather than subscription revenue), though EPAM has a base of large, long-tenured enterprise accounts that re-up engagements annually, giving revenue a semi-recurring character in aggregate even though individual statements of work are project-based.

revenue_streams.name: Other industry verticals (media, business info, emerging markets)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — large multinational corporations and select growth/scale-up clients; top clients are typically multi-year, multi-project relationships
business_model.geographic_mix: North America is the largest revenue geography, followed by Europe; delivery is heavily weighted to Central/Eastern Europe (including Ukraine, Belarus, Poland, Hungary), with growing delivery capacity in India, Latin America, and other nearshore/offshore hubs to diversify away from the CEE conflict zone

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-large cap pure-play digital engineering specialist; historically differentiated by deep, senior engineering talent (vs. high-volume/lower-skill offshore staffing models) and has been considered a premium/quality provider within the IT services space, though its historical geographic concentration in Ukraine/Belarus is both a differentiator (deep engineering talent pool) and a structural risk unique among large peers

moat_factors.description: Reputation for senior, highly-trained software engineers (historically sourced from strong STEM pipelines in Eastern Europe) supporting complex, high-value digital transformation work rather than commodity staff-augmentation

Long-tenured accounts with deep codebase and domain knowledge create switching costs, though competitive rebid risk exists at renewal given the project-based, non-contractual-lock-in nature of the business
One of the few IT services firms with delivery scale (~57,000 delivery professionals) combined with a consulting/experience-design layer (EPAM Continuum) for full life-cycle engagements
Strong reputation among enterprise CIOs for complex engineering execution, though brand strength is being tested by AI-driven pricing/productivity disruption narratives

weaknesses: No proprietary IP/software moat — the business model is fundamentally services/labor-based and thus vulnerable to margin compression from generative AI coding tools that reduce billable hours
Geographic delivery concentration risk in Ukraine/Belarus, both from an operational-continuity and reputational standpoint given the ongoing war
Low switching costs relative to product/platform businesses — client engagements can be rebid or insourced/brought to competitors at renewal
High client and industry concentration in cyclical, discretionary IT-spending categories (software/hi-tech, financial services) that pulled back sharply in 2022-2024 downcycle
Utilization/pricing model (largely time-and-materials) creates structural tension with AI-driven productivity gains that could shrink billable hours per project

growth_drivers: AI-native service lines: EPAM AI/RUN platform, DIALX Lab, and a multi-year strategic partnership with Anthropic (targeting 10,000+ Claude-certified architects) aimed at capturing AI-led transformation deals

Diversification of delivery footprint beyond Ukraine/Belarus into India, Latin America, Central Europe (Poland, Hungary) and other nearshore geographies to de-risk geopolitical exposure and access new talent pools
Recovery and reacceleration in Financial Services vertical (double-digit YoY growth in 2025-2026) as large banks resume digital transformation spending
Pipeline of large, multi-year AI-led enterprise deals expected to convert into meaningful revenue starting in H1 2027
Capital allocation shift toward shareholder returns — new $1 billion, 24-month share repurchase authorization (announced Oct 2025) alongside continued smaller tuck-in M&A
Cross-sell of EPAM Continuum consulting/experience-design capability to deepen existing large-account relationships beyond pure engineering delivery

business.description: Generative AI coding assistants can materially increase engineer productivity; because EPAM largely bills by the hour/FTE, faster code generation could shrink billable hours and pressure per-engagement revenue unless EPAM successfully repositions to outcome-based or higher-value AI-native pricing

The Software & Hi-Tech vertical, historically a top-2 vertical, has been in decline (down YoY in recent quarters) as tech clients cut discretionary engineering spend and increasingly build in-house or use AI tools directly
No long-term recurring contracts comparable to SaaS; large client losses or project cancellations can move revenue meaningfully quarter to quarter
Competition for skilled engineers, particularly amid geopolitical disruption to the CEE talent base, pressures compensation costs and utilization

financial.description: Operating margins have compressed from mid-teens historically to high-single/low-double digits in recent years amid demand softness, FX, and cost of maintaining bench capacity during downturns
Quarterly OCF/FCF has swung negative in several recent quarters (e.g., Q1 2026, H1 2026) reflecting working-capital timing and bonus/compensation payment cycles
Total debt increased from near-zero historically to ~$165M in Q1 2026 as EPAM began using debt alongside cash to fund accelerated share repurchases
Significant costs denominated in Eastern European, Indian, and Latin American currencies against USD-denominated client billing creates FX translation risk

regulatory.description: Belarus imposed restrictions (April 2024) on dividend distributions from Belarus-based entities to shareholders in certain countries including the U.S., complicating repatriation of cash held in-country (~$37M as of FY2025)

regulatory.risk: Immigration and visa policy (H-1B and similar)
regulatory.description: U.S. and European visa/work-permit policy changes could affect EPAM's ability to deploy talent across borders for onsite client engagements

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and cross-border data transfer regulation
regulatory.description: GDPR and similar regimes affect how client data can be processed by EPAM's global delivery centers

macro.description: ~14,100 of EPAM's personnel are based in Ukraine and Belarus as of FY2025; EPAM owns an office building in Kyiv and holds ~$39M and ~$37M of cash in Ukrainian and Belarusian banks respectively; an escalation involving Belarus directly, or renewed attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, could materially disrupt delivery capacity, damage facilities, and impair cash access

EPAM revenue is highly sensitive to enterprise technology budgets, which contract sharply in a slowing economy or during periods of macro uncertainty around rates/recession, as seen in the 2022-2024 downcycle
Management specifically cited a 'slow recovery in North America' as the reason for cutting FY2026 revenue guidance, pushing large AI-led deal conversion out to H1 2027

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The IT services/digital engineering industry is in a period of structural transition driven by generative AI: near-term demand is uneven (financial services recovering, software/hi-tech clients pulling back and building in-house AI tooling), while long-term industry growth increasingly depends on providers' ability to reposition from billable-hour staff augmentation toward higher-value, outcome-based AI transformation engagements
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — enterprise technology and digital transformation spending is discretionary and historically one of the first corporate budget lines cut in a downturn, as evidenced by EPAM's 2022-2024 revenue stagnation/decline
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity — higher rates reduce client capital available for large-scale digital transformation projects and increase EPAM's own cost of capital for its expanding buyback/debt program
key_input_costs: Cross-border FX (EUR, PLN, HUF, INR, BYN/UAH-adjacent costs vs. USD billing)
Real estate/office leases across delivery hubs

recent_developments.event: Reported Q2 2026 results: revenue of $1.415B (+4.5% YoY), GAAP diluted EPS $1.97 (+26.3% YoY), non-GAAP diluted EPS $3.38 (+22.0% YoY); GAAP operating margin improved to 10.8% from 9.3% YoY

Lowered full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 3.2%-4.2% (2.0%-3.0% organic constant currency) from prior guidance, citing slower-than-expected North American recovery; pushed meaningful AI-led large-deal revenue contribution out to H1 2027 from late 2026; shares fell sharply (reported ~16-22% single-day declines around guidance cuts during 2026)
Raised full-year profitability outlook toward the high end of the 15%-16% adjusted operating income margin range on cost discipline and H1 performance
Entered accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with Morgan Stanley for $300 million of common stock, part of the broader $1 billion buyback program
Completed a $223.5 million buyback (~1.16M shares) as part of capital return acceleration
Board authorized new $1 billion share repurchase program to be executed over 24 months

Expanded AI strategy via multi-year Anthropic partnership; launched EPAM AI/RUN platform and DIALX Lab; plans to build a practice of 10,000+ Claude-certified architects; over $105 million of AI-native revenue reported in a single quarter (Q1 2026 per management commentary)

Full-year 2025 revenue grew to $5.457B (+~15.5% YoY per reported metrics) with recovery led by Financial Services vertical (+~20% YoY in Q4); Software & Hi-Tech vertical showed a mixed/declining trend versus other verticals

Shares declined significantly through 2026 (roughly 45-50% peak-to-trough from ~$200+ early in the year to roughly $105-110 by late September 2026) amid investor concern that generative AI coding tools structurally threaten the billable-hours services model

items.notes: Cut from prior guidance due to slower-than-expected North American demand recovery
Reflects benefit of share buyback program on share count alongside operating performance
Buyback-driven EPS accretion partially offsets lowered revenue outlook
Raised on cost discipline and strong H1 2026 execution despite revenue guidance cut
Management guided to modest sequential growth in Q3, with flattish sequential revenue expected from Q3 into Q4

guidance.management_commentary: Management said large, multiyear AI-led enterprise deals in the pipeline are now expected to contribute meaningful revenue starting in the first half of 2027 rather than late 2026, pushing out the timeline investors had been anticipating. Demand is diverging by client type: financial services clients continue to increase spend (low-double-digit growth), while software and other tech clients have pulled back, partly reflecting those clients building AI capabilities in-house. Management continues to frame AI-native revenue (cited above $105 million in a recent quarter) as an emerging, fast-growing offset to legacy staff-augmentation pressure, while emphasizing capital return (buybacks) as a lever to support EPS even as top-line growth normalizes to mid-single digits.

bull_case: AI-native service lines (AI/RUN, DIALX Lab, Anthropic partnership) position EPAM to capture a new, faster-growing category of enterprise AI transformation spend rather than simply losing share to AI disruption

Aggressive $1 billion buyback program (a new, more aggressive capital-return posture versus EPAM's historically conservative balance sheet) is directly accretive to EPS and signals management's view that the ~45-50% stock decline in 2026 overstates the fundamental threat

Financial services vertical — EPAM's largest — is reaccelerating with double-digit growth, suggesting enterprise clients with complex legacy systems still need EPAM's deep engineering bench regardless of AI tooling

Valuation has reset materially (stock down roughly half from 2026 highs) while margins are improving, creating a more attractive entry point if AI fears prove overstated or EPAM successfully repositions its pricing model
Diversified, expanding delivery footprint outside Ukraine/Belarus (India, Latin America, other CEE) reduces the geopolitical tail risk that has weighed on the stock since 2022
bear_case: Generative AI coding tools pose a structural, not cyclical, threat to the time-and-materials billing model — if AI meaningfully cuts the hours needed per project, EPAM must sell proportionally more work just to hold revenue flat, and there is no proven pricing model yet that fully captures the productivity gain for EPAM rather than the client

Management has already pushed out the timeline for AI-led deals to convert into meaningful revenue (from late 2026 to H1 2027), and further delays or a failure to convert the pipeline would compound investor skepticism

Software & Hi-Tech vertical clients — arguably the most AI-savvy segment — are already pulling back and building in-house, which could be an early signal of how other verticals eventually behave as AI tooling matures

Ongoing Ukraine/Belarus war risk remains a unique tail risk among large-cap IT services peers, with real financial exposure (owned Kyiv office, tens of millions of cash trapped by Belarusian dividend restrictions) that could re-escalate at any time

Revenue growth has decelerated to mid-single digits (3-4% guided for FY2026) even as the company increases debt-funded buybacks, raising questions about capital allocation discipline if the core business does not stabilize
